report.summary: Chunk 3 of clones.py: implements near_clusters advisory Type-3 detection, safety-path heuristic, and _safety annotation.
risks: near_clusters | medium | Abstracting identifiers to ID can cause false near-clusters for low-entropy code; guards (exclude anonymous, min_shared_rare, max_cluster) are bounds not correctness. | Verify that the guards are sufficient to avoid excessive false positives in practice, e.g., with React/JSX codebases.

memo.put_abstract_fp | low | Assumption that 'whichever pass runs first pays' may lead to redundant re-abstraction if near_clusters runs before renamed_clusters but both need the fingerprint. | Confirm that renamed_clusters uses memo.get_abstract_fp to avoid re-tokenizing.

near_clusters | low | The docstring claims abstract fingerprint is 'free' here, but it still tokenizes twice per unit (once for bag, once for afp) as noted in comment. | Consider refactoring to avoid double tokenization.

near_clusters | low | The comment says 'output is unchanged by construction' but double tokenization could differ if _abstract_tokens has side effects or uses random state. | Verify _abstract_tokens is pure and deterministic.
near_clusters | low | The threshold float comparison uses >=, but floating-point may cause edge cases. | Ensure threshold comparison is robust (e.g., use math.isclose or tolerance).

near_clusters | low | The docstring claims clusters are 'Never auto-collapsed' but _safety returns 'judgment-gated — do NOT auto-collapse' only when safety paths are found; otherwise safety is None. | Clarify if 'Never auto-collapsed' means all near clusters are never auto-collapsed or only those with safety annotation.

_is_safety_path | medium | The import inside try/except may silently fail if sensitivity module is unavailable, causing paths to be missed. | Ensure GENERIC_HIGH_RISK_PATHS is always importable or handle failure explicitly.

handoff.purpose: Implements near_clusters advisory Type-3 clone detection, safety-path heuristic, and safety annotation.

symbols.name: near_clusters
symbols.note: Advisory Type-3 near-miss clusters using SourcererCC overlap on abstracted token bags; union-find grouping with guards; returns list of cluster dicts.

symbols.name: _HEURISTIC
symbols.note: Compiled regex matching safety-related path components (e.g., devices, drivers, firmware, kernel, safety, bias, interlock, relay, actuator).

symbols.name: _is_safety_path
symbols.note: Returns True if path matches safety heuristic or is in GENERIC_HIGH_RISK_PATHS (imported from sensitivity module).

symbols.name: _safety
symbols.note: Returns dict with safety annotation if any path in list is safety-related, else {'safety': None}.

claims.text: Advisory Type-3 (near-miss) clusters: units whose abstracted token bags overlap >= threshold but are NOT identical (exact/renamed cover those).
claims.why: Code filters out identical abstract fingerprints (afps[i] == afps[j]) and uses overlap >= threshold.

claims.text: Overlap is the SourcererCC multiset measure |A∩B| / |min(A,B)| on the abstracted bags.
claims.why: The _overlap function is not defined in this chunk, so the claim cannot be verified against this code.

claims.text: Union-find groups transitively similar units; each cluster carries similarity (mean pair overlap) + similarity_max.
claims.why: Code uses union-find (parent, size, find, union) and computes similarity as mean of overlaps, similarity_max as max.

claims.text: Never auto-collapsed (safety-annotated) — a heuristic, advisory only.
claims.why: Clusters include safety annotation from _safety; comment in _safety says 'do NOT auto-collapse'.

claims.text: abstracting every identifier to ID makes low-entropy code (React/JSX callbacks, thin API wrappers) look near-identical, and transitive union-find then chains such a family into one giant blob.
claims.why: Code includes guards to mitigate this: excludes anonymous lambdas, requires min_shared_rare non-ubiquitous tokens, caps cluster size at max_cluster.

claims.text: Three guards keep the signal actionable without changing the metric: (1) inline lambdas (<anonymous>) are excluded; (2) a pair must share >= min_shared_rare NON-ubiquitous tokens (incidental single-token matches don't chain); (3) a cluster stops growing past max_cluster members.
claims.why: Code: (1) filters u.name != _ANON; (2) checks len(rare[i] & rare[j]) < min_shared_rare; (3) union caps size[ra] + size[rb] > max_cluster.

claims.text: All three are bounds, not correctness — a Rust port must mirror them to reproduce the output.
claims.why: The guards are implemented as bounds (filters and caps) that affect output; mirroring them is necessary for reproducibility.

claims.text: Abstract ONCE and derive both. token_bag() and abstract_fingerprint() each call _abstract_tokens() internally, so calling both here tokenized the same source twice per unit -- the single largest piece of redundant work in the clone passes.
claims.why: Code calls _abstract_tokens once to get tokens, then creates bag and afp from that single call; comment explains that previously both functions would re-abstract.

claims.text: Output is unchanged by construction: the bag is the same Counter and the fingerprint comes from the same helper.
claims.why: Both bag and afp are derived from the same tokens list; no side effects.

claims.text: We tokenized for the bag anyway, so the abstract fingerprint was free here -- donate it so renamed_clusters need not re-abstract the same source. Whichever pass runs first pays; the other rides along.
claims.why: The claim about renamed_clusters re-using the fingerprint via memo.put_abstract_fp cannot be verified because renamed_clusters is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Rare tokens = those not saturating the corpus (drop ID/NUM/STR/common ops).
claims.why: Code computes document frequency df, then rare = {t for t in bag if df[t] <= ubiq_cut}, where ubiq_cut = max(3, int(0.4 * n)).
union function returns early if size[ra] + size[rb] > max_cluster.
The claim that identical clusters are covered elsewhere (e.g., by exact_clusters or renamed_clusters) cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: only incidental overlap -> not a real near-clone
claims.why: Code skips pairs with len(rare[i] & rare[j]) < min_shared_rare.
Code checks if not overlaps and continues, meaning only edges that were capped (union skipped) resulted in no overlaps.
The safety string in the returned dict includes this exact phrase.

observations.what: near_clusters uses _abstract_tokens once per unit to derive both bag and afp, avoiding double tokenization as noted in comment.
The union-find union function caps cluster growth at max_cluster by returning early if combined size exceeds limit.
The rare token set is computed per unit after filtering out ubiquitous tokens using document frequency with a floor of 3.
The _is_safety_path function imports GENERIC_HIGH_RISK_PATHS inside a try/except, which may silently ignore import errors.

The _safety function returns {'safety': None} if no safety paths found, but the docstring of near_clusters says 'Never auto-collapsed (safety-annotated)'. This could be misinterpreted as all near clusters are safety-annotated.
The near_clusters function filters out units with name == _ANON (anonymous), which is a guard against low-entropy inline lambdas.
